remote.definition: Far away from places where other people live; relating to work done from a location other than a traditional office.
remote.example: She prefers working in a remote location.

discipline.definition: The practice of training people to obey rules or a code of behavior; controlled behavior.
discipline.example: Learning a new language takes discipline.

flexibility.definition: The quality of bending easily without breaking; willingness to change or compromise.
flexibility.example: The job offers great flexibility in working hours.

productive.definition: Achieving a significant amount of results; producing a lot.
productive.example: I feel most productive in the morning.

boundary.definition: A line that marks the limits of an area; a dividing line.
boundary.example: It's important to set boundaries between work and life.

professional.definition: Relating to or connected with a profession; showing a high level of skill.
professional.example: She has a very professional approach to her work.

dedicated.definition: Devoted to a task or purpose; having strong feelings of support.

communication.definition: The imparting or exchanging of information by speaking, writing, or using other media.
communication.example: Good communication is key to teamwork.

colleague.definition: A person with whom one works, especially in a profession or business.
colleague.example: I discussed the project with my colleague.

environment.definition: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives or operates.
environment.example: A quiet environment helps me focus.

misunderstandings.definition: Failures to interpret something correctly; situations where something is misunderstood.

technology.definition: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry.
technology.example: Technology has changed the way we work.

artificial.definition: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally.

intelligence.definition: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.
intelligence.example: Emotional intelligence is important in leadership.

efficiently.definition: In a way that achieves maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort.
efficiently.example: She manages her time very efficiently.

productivity.definition: The effectiveness of productive effort; the rate of output per unit of input.
productivity.example: Our productivity increased after adopting new tools.

routine.definition: A sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.
routine.example: A morning routine helps me start the day well.

achievable.definition: Able to be brought about or reached successfully.
achievable.example: Set small, achievable goals every day.

commute.definition: A regular journey of some distance to and from one's place of work.
commute.example: My daily commute takes about an hour.

lifestyle.definition: The way in which a person or group lives.
lifestyle.example: Remote work can lead to a healthier lifestyle.

mastering.definition: Acquiring complete knowledge or skill in something.
mastering.example: Mastering a language requires daily practice.

schedule.definition: A plan for carrying out a process or procedure.
schedule.example: I need to check my schedule for tomorrow.

signal.definition: A gesture, action, or sound that is used to convey information or instructions.
signal.example: Closing your laptop can signal that your workday is over.

stress.definition: A state of mental or emotional strain resulting from demanding circumstances.
stress.example: Exercise is a good way to reduce stress.
